items.summary: This preprint presents PCCG-2, an engineered continuation-control architecture that separates frozen answer capability from learned prerequisite-conditioned permission in a composite Qwen3-4B system. The content model receives only a question and remains completely frozen; a separate 101-parameter gate receives only a six-digit equality condition and can modify only the native end-of-sequence (EOS) logit at the first generated token. Every non-EOS logit remains unchanged. A deterministic stock-capability procedure fixes a bank of 188 questions before permission training. Condition qualification and condition FINAL each pass 65,536/65,536 cases, while combined FINAL passes 2,048/2,048 contexts spanning 75 answer identities and 188/188 question-only controls remain unchanged. A bidirectional causal intervention reverses answer to EOS in 40/40 cases and EOS to the corresponding correct answer in 40/40 cases across 40 answer identities, with 80/80 matched sham controls unchanged. In the canonical five-arm witness, the score of token “4” remains exactly 53.0 and the complete non-EOS first-token logit vector is byte-identical while the generated outcome switches between the answer and native EOS. Separately, a finite-precision proof certifies the baseline continuation rule for every accepted six-digit equality condition paired with each of the 188 frozen bank computations under the stated numerical environment, covering 810,000,000,000 ordered condition pairs. The result demonstrates an explicit architectural separation between what the frozen model would answer and whether that unchanged answer is permitted to enter generation. It does not claim discovery of a naturally occurring permission circuit in stock Qwen, arbitrary-predicate generalization, general alignment, or control of consequential external actions. The frozen model, source, experimental evidence, and inference replay procedures are available in the linked Hugging Face release. This Zenodo record contains the paper and manuscript supplement, including the proof checker, certificate, artifact index, and public-copy replay receipt.

items.summary: Frequency-shift corrections are applied in deep-space navigation as a catalogue of formulas: common offsets, detector-end $O(c^{-3})$ cross terms and the nonlinear Doppler bias are re-derived for every mission and every data type. This paper derives the structure itself, from a single transitivity axiom. Under that axiom the endpoint factor of any light-path observable is a ratio of generators --- the \textbf{Fuxi value} $\FX_{A\|B}=\alpha_A/\alpha_B$ --- multiplied by a path factor; the generator is identified with the rate of proper-time flow, $\alpha_X=\mathrm d\tau_X/\mathrm dt_{\rm GalST}$. The resulting framework (Fuxi-ratio Mapping Theory, hereafter FMT) leaves the path-dependent transfer factor $\Pi_{\rm TTF}$ with the full complexity of the null-geodesic boundary-value problem, while its $1$PN expansion reproduces the standard frequency-shift formulas term by term at $O(c^{-2})$ and endows the IAU conversion constants $L_C,L_G,L_B$ with a direct generator interpretation. Three consequences are closed-form. \textbf{(i)} The projected pulsar-Doppler residual is \emph{exactly} linear in the relativistic velocity $\mathbf u\equiv\gamma\mathbf v$: the $O(c^{-3})$ kinematic term of the coordinate-velocity parameterization is a parameterization effect with the exact closed form $v_D^3/(2c^2)\,\hat{\mathbf v}_D$, removable in one analytic step, and \emph{identically absent} under $\mathbf u$. \textbf{(ii)} Isotropic and dipolar residual components are absorbed exactly --- the latter as a velocity error independent of the pulsar number and of the network geometry. \textbf{(iii)} Residuals of angular order $\ell\ge2$ are \emph{not} absorbed; their leakage is fixed by the higher moments of the pulsar directions, so precision and bias immunity are governed by different moments of the same network. Velocity identifiability is necessary and sufficient: the pulsar directions must not be cocircular. Model-internal consistency tests with a realistic 16-pulsar IPTA geometry reach $16.1\ \mu$m/s (three-axis RMS) at ideal timing precision $\sigma_\delta=10^{-13}$, and a full Earth-departure-to-Mars-surface arc is closed by the same expression with only its inputs changed. Both statements are model-internal limits: the term-by-term agreement with the standard formulas is limited to $O(c^{-2})$, the velocity figures presuppose an ephemeris residual $\delta C_P\lesssim3\times10^{-14}$, and practical accuracy is bounded by clock, ephemeris and direction knowledge. FMT modifies neither general relativity nor observational hardware: it is an algebraic interface callable on existing ephemerides and timing data.
items.title: Relativistic Doppler Velocimetry from One Transitivity Axiom: Exact Bias and Identifiability

items.summary: Adaptability release: sqzcomb now speaks laboratory units and fits measured data, so the normalized-units engine underneath is usable directly from an experiment. RingSpec (loaded linewidth in Hz, escape efficiency, single-photon Kerr shift, pump wavelength -- with a mandatory reference naming where the numbers come from) plus normalized_pump , threshold_power , normalized_detuning , normalized_dispersion , normalized_frequency / physical_frequency , and intracavity_photons . Conventions are checked by identities rather than trusted: every conversion round-trips exactly, F scales as sqrt(P), and threshold_power is cross-validated through the package's own flat-state cubic -- at the returned power, homogeneous_steady_states contains the rho = 1 root to machine precision. Physical constants come from scipy.constants ; no constant is typed by hand. sqzcomb.fitnoise : extraction of (mu, eta, kappa) from measured homodyne noise spectra in dB relative to shot noise -- the standard characterization of a below-threshold squeezer. fit_noise_spectra fits the package's own input-output model (the same code path as sqzcomb.spectra , cross-checked in the tests against the independent closed form) to the squeezed/antisqueezed trace pair, with an optional white dark-noise floor and per-point measurement sigmas enabling a chi-square consistency check. Identifiability is enforced, not hoped for: one quadrature alone is a single Lorentzian with two shape numbers for three unknowns, so the single-trace fit is refused unless an independently measured kappa_hz is supplied; an antisqueezed trace systematically below shot noise is refused as unphysical. Changed scipy is now a declared dependency (the new modules use scipy.constants and scipy.optimize.least_squares ). Anchors (asserted in tests/test_adapt.py , not stated) Conversion round trips exact to 1e-15; F(4P) = 2F(P); at fixed eta_esc, doubling kappa halves F. threshold_power hits the rho = 1 root of the package's own cubic for alpha in {0.7, 1.0, 1.8}. Noise-free synthetic spectra return the generating (mu, eta, kappa) to better than 1e-6; the fitted model equals the closed form S = 0.5[1 -/+ 4 eta mu / ((1 +/- mu)^2 + Omega^2)] at every frequency to 1e-10. Seeded Monte-Carlo scatter of the fitted parameters matches the reported one-sigma uncertainties; a dark floor deliberately omitted from the model biases eta, and fitting it recovers the truth. The under-determined single-trace case and the impossible below-shot-noise antisqueezed trace are refused with explanatory errors. Full test suite: 80 passed. See CHANGELOG.md for details.

items.summary: We present a synthesis of the Karimov–Alekberli (KA) Framework into a unified theory of Constitutional Intelligence: the capacity of an adaptive system to make consequential decisions that are simultaneously governed, explainable, accountable, reconstructable, verifiable, and capable of learning without retroactive falsification of the historical record. We formulate six formal results — one per required property — organized into three proof tiers: Tier A (two unconditional geometric results), Tier B (three conditional results valid under explicit identifiability and compactness assumptions), Tier C (one KA extension under a physical implementation assumption). Results draw on viability theory,information geometry, and thermodynamics. The theorems are organized in three tiers reflecting their current proof status: Tier A (fully proved geometric results), Tier B (conditional theorems under explicit identifiability and compactness assumptions), and Tier C (KA extensions requiring additional physical or topological conditions). A unifying condition, the Constitutional Integrity Criterion (CIC), is formulated as a representation theorem characterizing systems that satisfy all six properties simultaneously. We derive, under the CIC, that the governance loop Govern → Reason → Act → Remember → Learn → Govern defines a well-defined autonomous map on the constitutional moduli space that preserves the admissible region; fixed-point existence follows as a corollary under compactness. We position the framework within the existing literature on viability theory, formal verification, safe reinforcement learning, AI governance, and constitutional economics. We propose Constitutional Intelligence Science as the emerging discipline that unifies these results.
items.title: Constitutional Intelligence as Formal Science The Karimov–Alekberli Framework as Mathematical Foundation for Governed Institutional Cognition

items.summary: A dictionary-first harmonisation tool for aligning constructs across five longitudinal youth-development cohorts — LSAC (Growing Up in Australia), ABCD, TESS (Trondheim Early Secure Study), Ten to Men and LSIC (Footprints in Time) — using variable-level metadata only, with no access to participant data and no redistribution of dictionary files. Cohorts and target constructs are configuration rather than code, so the tool generalises to constructs and cohorts beyond the anxiety application it was built for. Four adapters cover the dictionary shapes encountered, including inventories built from published documentation for cohorts with no custodian codebook; every row records the tier of evidence it rests on, distinguishing a custodian dictionary from a published cohort profile from a reconstruction assembled from methods sections. Outputs: a construct coverage matrix over primary waves; a register of constructs declared non-harmonisable, each with a mandatory stated reason and empirical confirmation of absence; an assessment, for every cohort pair, of whether genuine common items exist to anchor a multi-group latent model or whether the inference must be harmonised instead of the scale; a check that the cohorts holding a construct agree on who reported it; and an audit of published methodological claims against the cohorts' own dictionaries. Verdicts are evidence-tier aware. A cohort read from a custodian dictionary can contradict a claim; a cohort inventoried from publications can only fail to confirm one, and is reported as unverifiable rather than false. A declared absence is confirmed only for cohorts where a dictionary exists to confirm it in. Data governance is enforced in code rather than described in prose: a governed cohort is excluded unless explicitly included, its culturally grounded wellbeing indicators cannot be mapped as standing in for a diagnostic construct, and a non-harmonisable declaration without a stated reason raises an error. Provenance records a SHA-256 over every dictionary read, so a third party can confirm they ran against the same releases without those files being redistributed.

items.summary: Timely urban-canopy information is essential for linking remote sensing with heat, mobility, and neighborhood planning. We developed an optical GeoAI workflow for Davis, California, using 2022 National Agriculture Imagery Program imagery (0.6 m RGB+NIR). DeepForest generated crown candidates; an NDVI threshold, non-maximum suppression, and box-prompted Segment Anything Model (ViT-B) produced a crown-anchored canopy surface. Analyses used the 25.92 km2 Census TIGER municipal boundary and a 100 m grid. The workflow retained 11,741 candidate crowns and mapped 7.71 km2 of canopy (29.8% of the city). On the identical extent, pixel precision was 0.804, pixel recall was 0.873, and 97.4% of candidate centers agreed with the 2022 USDA/CAL FIRE LiDAR-assisted canopy product (IoU 0.719; Dice 0.837; area recovery 108.5%). Approximately 49% of candidates occurred within 15 m of a road. Canopy was inversely associated with Landsat land-surface temperature (Spearman rho = -0.477; partial rho = -0.551 controlling for built probability), and spatial-lag modeling confirmed clear neighborhood structure. Two transparent attention surfaces combined canopy need with thermal and contextual indicators. The framework provides a reproducible, updateable screening layer that complements structural canopy products and municipal inventories while retaining assumptions, data provenance, and spatial diagnostics for planning interpretation.
items.title: From crown candidates to neighborhood screening: integrating optical GeoAI and spatial modeling for urban-canopy assessment in Davis, California

items.summary: Determinism and numerical reproducibility are increasingly required of GPU kernels in machine learning systems, yet deterministic implementations of the same kernel can still differ bit for bit. Floating-point reduction order is the primary cause, alongside partial-sum precision, fused multiply-add operations, and rounding placement. These choices may be hand-coded, selected by a block-level language such as Triton, or hidden inside a closed-source library such as cuBLAS or rocBLAS. A tile shape chosen for performance therefore also determines the arithmetic, potentially breaking batch invariance. Preserving a fixed order can cost up to 20 percent, while an autotuner cannot identify which configurations are bitwise equivalent. We characterize the factors determining the bitwise behavior of reductions and general matrix multiplication (GEMM). First, we introduce a descriptor of GEMM reduction order, including the partitioning of K in split-K GEMM. Using it, we perform the first black-box reconstruction of a closed-source library's arithmetic for bit-level correctness. Our family of Triton GEMMs matches NVIDIA cuBLAS in all tested cases on Blackwell and Hopper. For realistic LLM shapes with fused epilogues, it matches or exceeds torch.compile performance. Second, we enforce balanced-tree reduction during Triton lowering and introduce a data-layout optimization that brings 19 of 27 kernels on GB300 and H100 within 10 percent of free-order performance. Third, we develop sound static checkers for bitwise equivalence between compiled GPU kernels, including the first checker spanning NVIDIA PTX and AMD GCN. Integrated into Triton's autotuner, the checker restricts search to a single bit-equivalence class.
items.title: Taming Bitwise Behavior in GPU Kernels with Tensor Core: Black-Box Reconstruction, Compiler Enforcement, and Static Verification

items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable progress, yet their massive storage and memory-bandwidth demands still hinder efficient deployment. Weight binarization is a promising solution, but existing binarization-based post-training quantization (PTQ) methods usually far exceed the nominal 1-bit storage target due to hidden overhead. To address this gap, we propose All for 1-Bit (AF1), a genuine 1-bit PTQ framework for LLMs. AF1 comprises two complementary components: (1) Null-space-Aware Binary Factorization (NABF) for improving binary reconstruction through Hessian-aware surrogate reparameterization, null-space-aware binary factorization, and scale-only global reconstruction; and (2) Hierarchical Shapley Allocation (HiSA) for assigning structural capacity using hierarchical Shapley sensitivity. Together, they preserve model accuracy under a strict 1.0-BPW budget in the PTQ setting. Experiments on LLaMA, Qwen, and Gemma families show that AF1 consistently outperforms existing binarization-based PTQ methods in perplexity and zero-shot accuracy. Compared with BF16, AF1 achieves an average 2.5 times inference speedup and over 90% memory reduction across evaluated models, providing a practical path toward deployable genuine 1-bit compression for LLMs. The code for reproducibility is available at https://github.com/Kishon-zzx/AF1.
items.title: All for 1-Bit: Towards Genuine 1-Bit Post-Training Quantization for LLMs

items.summary: NTI (Non-Termination Inference) is an open-source Java tool for proving termination and non-termination of term rewrite systems and logic programs. This reproducibility capsule accompanies the manuscript “NTI: Non-Termination Analysis for Term Rewriting and Logic Programming”. The capsule archives NTI version 2026.09, exactly as published at GitHub commit 88a47f9db976fc7c1ad1921057f0a68d68748137. It includes the complete source code, an executable JAR, compilation and usage documentation, license notices, and the corresponding sources of the bundled SAT4J Core 2.3.6 dependency. No additional source patch is required. Nine examples support reproduction of the manuscript: three illustrative examples and six instances from its Impact table. Their input files, expected verdicts, reference outputs and provenance are included. A Python runner executes the examples with time limits and records the results. The REPRODUCING.md file explains the workflow, and SHA-256 checksums allow file integrity verification. An optional Dockerfile builds the software from source with Java 21. All 888 tests passed with the standard Maven configuration, both on macOS arm64 with Java 24 and on Docker Linux arm64 with Temurin Java 21.0.12. All nine example verdicts were reproduced in both environments; the Docker example runs required no network access. No tests were skipped. Build and execution reports are included. Java 21 or later is required to run the supplied JAR. Docker and Python are optional conveniences; no prebuilt Docker image is included. The capsule reproduces the selected manuscript examples, but does not rerun all historical competition experiments or establish the full historical regression coverage.

items.summary: PGAA is an executable claim-state compiler for perturbation transcriptomics. It combines internal decision state, ranking stability, external evidence, source-data provenance, and branch-specific promotion gates to emit bounded manuscript claim states, so that an exploratory signal cannot be promoted to a biological or translational conclusion without the evidence a promotion rule requires. Distribution-aware statistics (a Wasserstein statistic for full expression-distribution shifts and a histogram-shape statistic for responder-associated expression-shape changes) are retained as upstream scoring modules that supply scores to the compiler; they are not claimed as the main methodological novelty. This archive is a code-only software release and excludes manuscript drafts, submission materials, figures, source-data tables, and review materials.
items.title: PGAA: a claim-state compiler for perturbation-transcriptomic evidence

items.summary: This record contains the first Lean-verified certificate in the Quantum–Classical Shared-Time working formalization series. Q1 establishes a common real-time mathematical structure for quantum and classical evolution. The certificate places both systems on the same time domain, formally represents their evolving states and time derivatives, and proves that when quantum and classical states correspond through an observation map at every time, their accumulated change between two times also corresponds exactly. The formalization includes normalized quantum-state evolution, classical phase-state evolution, shared-time structure, derivative uniqueness, and an orientation-independent change result that works in either direction between two times. This first milestone is intentionally foundational. It establishes the formal structure needed for the later quantum-to-classical bridge without yet assuming the Schrödinger equation, Ehrenfest theorem, Newtonian dynamics, or the later Chronos connection. The next stage is to formalize quantum expectation values and their time evolution as the next step toward a machine-checked Ehrenfest bridge connecting accepted quantum mechanics with accepted classical physics. This deposit is part of an ongoing formal validation program. The certificate package includes Lean source, reproducibility instructions, dependency and provenance documentation, build information, axiom audits, and checksums. The formal build passes without sorry, admit, or sorryAx placeholders.
items.title: Lean-Verified Quantum–Classical Shared-Time Bridge — Working Formal Verification Series Q1 (v0.1)

items.summary: This white paper examines the commercial cost created when customers question the human care, originality, factual integrity, provenance, or accountability behind AI-assisted brand interactions. It defines this cost as the Authenticity Tax: a cumulative drag on conversion, retention, customer trust, escalation cost, reputational equity, and long-term brand value. Unlike visible rejection or service failure, authenticity-related doubt often remains silent, influencing customer behaviour without producing a clear complaint or attribution signal. The paper identifies six commercial components of the Authenticity Tax: Conversion Drag, Verification Friction, Human Escalation Cost, Correction and Rework, Reputational Discount, and Lost Trust Compounding. It also identifies five structural causes: Provenance Ambiguity, the Effort Discount, the Intentionality Gap, Accountability Diffusion, and Voice Convergence. Together, these mechanisms explain why lower production costs do not automatically translate into higher net value when AI-generated communication reduces customer confidence or perceived care. Case studies covering Air Canada, CNET, and Amazon illustrate three distinct operating patterns. Air Canada demonstrates accountability risk when automated customer guidance conflicts with policy. CNET demonstrates the correction and portfolio-level credibility cost created by weak disclosure and editorial controls. Amazon demonstrates the opposite strategy: investing proactively in authenticity, fraud prevention, review integrity, and trust infrastructure at scale. The paper introduces the Authenticity Proof Stack, comprising Provenance, Accountability, Originality, Contextual Care, Transparency, and Recourse. It also proposes a Human-Care Threshold that matches human involvement to consequence, ranging from AI-first reversible interactions to human-led high-stakes decisions. A Net AI Value equation incorporates Gross Automation Benefit, Authenticity Tax, and Governance Cost to provide a more complete commercial assessment of AI deployment. The central proposition is that authenticity is becoming an operating condition rather than a stylistic brand attribute. In an environment where competent communication becomes abundant, trust increasingly depends on verifiable evidence, visible accountability, original knowledge, appropriate human judgment, and effective recourse.   Originally published on LoganSivanasen.com on 4 August 2026.

items.summary: This preprint presents PCCG-2, an engineered continuation-control architecture that separates frozen answer capability from learned prerequisite-conditioned permission in a composite Qwen3-4B system. The content model receives only a question and remains completely frozen; a separate 101-parameter gate receives only a six-digit equality condition and can modify only the native end-of-sequence (EOS) logit at the first generated token. Every non-EOS logit remains unchanged. A deterministic stock-capability procedure fixes a bank of 188 questions before permission training. Condition qualification and condition FINAL each pass 65,536/65,536 cases, while combined FINAL passes 2,048/2,048 contexts spanning 75 answer identities and 188/188 question-only controls remain unchanged. A bidirectional causal intervention reverses answer to EOS in 40/40 cases and EOS to the corresponding correct answer in 40/40 cases across 40 answer identities, with 80/80 matched sham controls unchanged. In the canonical five-arm witness, the score of token “4” remains exactly 53.0 and the complete non-EOS first-token logit vector is byte-identical while the generated outcome switches between the answer and native EOS. Separately, a finite-precision proof certifies the baseline continuation rule for every accepted six-digit equality condition paired with each of the 188 frozen bank computations under the stated numerical environment, covering 810,000,000,000 ordered condition pairs. The result demonstrates an explicit architectural separation between what the frozen model would answer and whether that unchanged answer is permitted to enter generation. It does not claim discovery of a naturally occurring permission circuit in stock Qwen, arbitrary-predicate generalization, general alignment, or control of consequential external actions. The frozen model, source, experimental evidence, and inference replay procedures are available in the linked Hugging Face release. This Zenodo record contains the paper and manuscript supplement, including the proof checker, certificate, artifact index, and public-copy replay receipt.

items.summary: Satellite-derived bathymetry (SDB) from multispectral imagery is cost-effective but scales poorly across regions, especially in optically complex coastal environments. We evaluate machine learning and deep learning for transferable SDB over the 0-20 m depth range using Sentinel-2 imagery. A Random Forest baseline and four CNNs (ResNet-50, ResNet-101, EfficientNet-B4, ConvNeXt-Large) are trained on Pratas Island and selected Great Barrier Reef regions, then evaluated on spatially independent intra- and cross-regional test areas. Preserving spatial continuity during training, by keeping contiguous reef blocks rather than random patches, is the single most impactful design choice; we further introduce a Smooth Weight Function (SWF)-weighted RMSE loss that emphasizes near-surface depths. With these choices, intra-regional RMSE ranges from 1.15 to 1.92 m over 0-20 m and is as low as 0.26 m for depths <= 3 m. Random Forest degrades sharply under cross-regional transfer (RMSE 1.53 m -> 2.99-3.78 m), while the deep models stay more robust (2.46-2.98 m). On the public MagicBathyNet aerial-RGB benchmark (0-16 m) the proposed networks reach 0.19-0.22 m RMSE, outperforming a U-Net baseline and a task-specific transformer architecture with substantially fewer parameters. We further exploit multi-temporal repeat imagery: training on it broadens diversity, and median-aggregating predictions across passes at inference reduces noise from changing sun angles, atmospheric conditions, water properties, and tides. We release optimized architectures and pretrained weights to enable scalable transfer to new sites.
items.title: From Local Training to Large-Scale Mapping: A Comparative Assessment of Machine Learning and Deep Learning for Transferable Satellite-Derived Bathymetry

items.summary: Repeated in-situ evaluation of ocean-glider planners requires scarce vehicles, operators, deployment and recovery resources, and ocean conditions that cannot be reset for competing algorithms. We present a guided, installation-free browser-native digital test range that transforms a selected region into a reproducible four-dimensional experiment. The system leads users from regional domain selection through mission-scoped bathymetry, time/depth forcing, science objectives, optional task decomposition, route specification, current-advected execution, observation generation, and scoring. Its primary contribution is a common plan-to-observation contract unifying vehicle, sensing, and evaluator assumptions across manual routes, transparent built-in algorithms, and imported classical or learned-planner outputs, while exported artifacts form dataset-ready records. A controlled Observing System Simulation Experiment (OSSE) evaluates five classical planners in two episodes, three deterministic seeds, and a calibrated 60-hour horizon. All 54 missions completed and recovered without hard violations, while planner rankings and dive-policy effects revealed operational-scientific tradeoffs. An authentic public deployment supplied a field-referenced audit to scope current kinematic boundaries. Separately, source-locked GliderFlight 1.2.0 achieved native-to-browser parity through Pyodide/WebAssembly, establishing a pathway for high-fidelity multi-tier simulation. The resulting operational space is scientifically traceable and component-qualified for mission-scale pre-deployment experimentation.

items.summary: Whether a neural language model can report facts about its own computation is difficult to evaluate because an accurate report may be generated either from the realized runtime state or from a static simulation of the computation conditioned on the input and fixed parameters. We formalize this distinction and show that, under deterministic inference, an internal property of an unperturbed forward pass is not by itself sufficient to distinguish these mechanisms: the realized state is an exact deterministic function of the static input and parameters.  We introduce the Exogenous State Watermark (ESW), a controlled intervention protocol in which an externally sampled perturbation is injected into an intermediate representation while the model's observable next-token output is audited for greedy invariance. For the isolated watermark bit, the static information set has a 50% Bayes-optimal chance bound under the stated independence assumptions. For the counterfactual target, we evaluate unperturbed-state and runtime representations empirically on GPT-2 (124M parameters; width 768).
